title: Higher endomorphism-bundle cohomology vanishing for strongly amply stable coprime quiver moduli over algebraically closed characteristic-zero fields
source_title: Rigidity and Schofield’s partial tilting conjecture for quiver moduli
author: Pieter Belmans; Ana-Maria Brecan; Hans Franzen; Gianni Petrella; Markus Reineke
difficulty_reason: Teleman quantization alone cannot yield the vanishing until every unstable stratum has a strict window bound for the universal endomorphism summands. The authors compute the equivariant determinant width through the normal/relative tangent sequences and identify the universal-bundle fiber weights under the HN one-parameter subgroups. They then turn strong ample stability into the required strict inequality across all HN types, providing the nonroutine uniform window verification beyond the precise prior GIT/quantization foundations.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Algebraically closed base field of characteristic zero; finite quiver, theta-coprime dimension vector d with theta(d)=0, and strongly amply theta-stable d as Definition4.1. Higher cohomology of every Ui-dual tensor Uj vanishes. Acyclicity is not required for this selected vanishing. Full new equivariant window and bundle-weight calculations18–23, strict inequality26–27 and main proof27 read; moduli/universal normalization and Hesselink–Harder–Narasimhan data8–17 read. Teleman/Halpern-Leistner quantization13–14 and published Reineke, Hoskins and Zamora strata results are named prerequisites. No rigidity corollary, weakened conjectural stability condition, twisted-bundle variant or examples separately counted. Full original36 physical pages preserved.

historical_source_pdf_evidence.original_difficulty_reason: The authors compute equivariant conormal window widths and universal-bundle weights along Harder–Narasimhan strata, prove a strict slope/Euler-pairing inequality and apply quantization to establish partial tilting. These derived and invariant-theoretic constructions exceed ordinary qualifying exams.
